gap_fill_decisions: strength = ATR-normalised 1h displacement vs USD; momentum direction chosen because 'relative strength' conventionally means long strong / short weak (the registry does not state the direction)
relative position = two USD-pair legs, each 0.25% risk, so the pair-trade totals the standard 0.5%
missing_in_source: position-sizing rule (supplied by the EUR 500 capital model of this task)
single outcome horizon (registry lists candidate sets only)
cost model (supplied by the shared harness)
direction (momentum vs reversal) of the relative position
how a 'relative position' is built from the available pairs
name: FAST -- Cross-Currency Relative Strength

operationalization.entry: both legs market at next-open; all-or-nothing (if either leg fails any gate neither is sent)
exits: either leg's stop closes only that leg's position (the other continues to its own exit)
time exit of both legs at the first 15m boundary >= signal bar close + 60 min
operationalization.rule: For each pair p: m_p = (C_t - C_{t-4}) / (ATR14_p * sqrt(4)) (A3). Non-USD currency strength s_c = +m_p where the currency is the BASE (EUR, GBP, AUD, NZD vs USD) and -m_p where it is the QUOTE (JPY, CHF, CAD in USDJPY, USDCHF, USDCAD). If max(s) - min(s) >= 3.0: BUY the strongest currency vs USD and SELL the weakest currency vs USD (USD-neutral relative position, two pair legs).

source_registry.note: introduces currency-exposure netting considerations more directly than any other FAST family
source_registry.original_signal_definition: CONCEPT ONLY: rank currencies by short-horizon relative strength and take relative (not outright) positions. No formula frozen.
source_registry.required_data: 1-minute canonical FX bars across the full candidate universe simultaneously (common-timestamp alignment).
